Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

interest noun

a liking for something

also be interested in, interested, keen on, go in for, I don’t go in for sports, I am interested in that, that book is interesting, interesting, have an interest in, take an interest in, interest (someone), sports don’t interest me

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.33.3: piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur
Cic. Fin. 5.5
M-O s.v. interest vb.
Traupman 333

studium, studiī n.

noun, second declension

interest, keenness; a pursuit

With the genitive of the thing. “It interests me” is mē tenet, it holds me: ille liber mē tenet, that book is interesting (Traupman 101); philosophiae studium mē tenet (Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • studeō, studēre, studuī — be interested in, be keen on (+ dative)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 101: mūsicae studeō, I am interested in music; M-O s.v. interest vb.; Traupman 99: lūdīs nōn studeō; Traupman 101: mūsicae studeō; Traupman 322; Traupman 334

  • studiōsus, studiōsa, studiōsum — keen on, interested in (+ genitive)

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 74: vēnandī aut pilae studiōsī

  • teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — interest, hold the attention of

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 334

    What interests one holds one: ille liber mē tenet; in the passive, studiō tenērī, to be keen on (Plin. Ep. 9.33.3, above).

Examples

  • omnis hīc aetās piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur

    everyone here, young and old, is keen on fishing, sailing and swimming tooPlin. Ep. 9.33.3

  • suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur

    for each of us is led most by his own interestsCic. Fin. 5.5

  • studium pingendī habēre

    to have an interest in paintingTraupman 333

  • studiō alicujus reī tenērī

    to take an interest in somethingTraupman 333

  • Lūdī mē nōn tenent.

    Sports don’t interest me.Traupman 334

  • Līberī lūdīs tenentur.

    Children are interested in games.Traupman 334

  • Circēnsibus nē levissimē quidem teneor.

    I am not the least bit interested in the races.Traupman 334

  • Ille liber mē tenet.

    That book is interesting.Traupman 334

See also interest, interest, curious.
